entries.title: Can Federated IID and Non-IID training for datasets with various censoring rates be simplified to a single batch size?
entries.question: I am working with a benchmark comparison of federated survival models. My plan is to experiment with these models on centralized, IID and non-IID settings. I have already distributed global training, validation and test data among 5 clients. Each client’s data consists of 5 folds. 3 folds are used to train the model, 1 fold is used as a validation set and another fold is used as a test fold. For global Learning, I train the survival model using this process: i) Calculate forward pass on a batch ii) Calculate loss and get gradient for that batch iii) Apply the gradients to update the network iv) Repeat For Federated Learning (FL), I am using this process: i) Use client devices/data to calcul...
entries.answer: Your results are actually not wrong, but the assumption that centralized > IID > Non-IID is a heuristic, not a law. Maybe these are the cases: 1. Implicit Regularization from Federated Averaging Each federated round averages gradients across 5 clients, which acts like an ensemble effect. This can reduce overfitting, especially on small datasets (3241 rows is not large for survival analysis). 2. Your Batch Size is Likely Too Large for Centralized With 3241 samples, 3 training folds ≈ ~1944 samples. A batch size of 64 means only ~30 gradient updates per epoch. In federated settings, each client trains on ~389 samples with batch 64, giving ~6 updates per client per round — but aggregated across 5 clients, the effective gradient diversity is higher. 3. Early Stopping Asymmetry Centralized: 25-epoch patience on the full model Federated: 25-epoch patience at both server and client level The federated model gets two regularization signals, which can be beneficial. 4. Censoring Rate Interaction (38.72%) The UnempDur dataset has ~38.72% censored observations. Federated splitting can accidentally create better-stratified censoring distributions per client, improving the C-Index signal. entries.title: How accurate are modern AI content detectors?
entries.question: Is there a report on how accurate are modern (2024 and beyond) AI-generated content detectors?
entries.answer: It's an entire field of research. A few pointers: 2024 papers with many citations: MAGE. Li et al., ACL 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13242 . 447k generations from 27 LLMs across 10 domains; foundational in-the-wild generalization benchmark. RAID. Dugan et al., ACL 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07940 . 6.2M-generation adversarial benchmark; "99% accurate" detectors collapse under attacks/unseen generators. M4GT-Bench. Wang et al., ACL 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11175 . Multilingual, multi-domain, multi-generator benchmark with span-level boundary detection (basis of SemEval-2024 Task 8). Perkins et al., 2024 ("GenAI Detection Tools, Adversarial Techniques..."). Int. J. Ed. Tech. in Higher Ed. https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19148 . Six commercial detectors at 39.5% baseline accuracy, dropping 17.4% under simple adversarial manipulation. DF40. Yan et al., NeurIPS 2024 D&B. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13495 . 40 distinct deepfake generation techniques across face-swap/reenactment/synthesis/editing; cross-generator generalization benchmark. DetectRL. Wu et al., NeurIPS 2024 D&B. https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.23746 . Real-world adversarial benchmark in abuse-prone domains; SOTA detectors underperform under prompt attacks, paraphrasing, perturbations. More recent papers from 2025–2026: Deepfake-Eval-2024. Chandra et al., TrueMedia.org/UW, March 2025. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.0...

entries.title: 怎样做一个每天汇总优质 AI 问答并发布到 GitHub 的平台？
entries.question: 我想让 agent 每天搜集用户向 AI 提出的优质问题和回答，提交到我的 GitHub 上，并且可以在 public network 上查看。这个东西应该怎么设计？
entries.answer: 最小可行版本可以分成三层：内容入口、审核整理、公开展示。内容入口负责收集候选问答，可以来自手动 JSON、GitHub Issue、表单、浏览器插件或聊天导出，但必须先做授权和匿名化。审核整理层负责给每条问答补标题、摘要、标签、模型、质量理由，并过滤掉隐私、低质量和不可公开内容。公开展示层用 GitHub Pages 发布静态站点，仓库保存原始 curated 数据、每日构建出的 JSON 和 Markdown。每天的自动化任务只做两件事：把新增候选转成规范数据，再重新构建 public 目录并提交。这样它既像知乎一样能浏览和归档，又保留 GitHub 的版本历史和公共可见性。
entries.summary: 把平台拆成内容入口、审核整理和公开展示三层，用 GitHub Pages 做可公开访问的知识库。
quality_signals: 问题明确提出了自动化、GitHub 留痕和公开访问三个产品约束。
回答给出可落地架构，而不是停留在概念层。
适合作为平台第一条元问题，解释这个项目本身为什么存在。

entries.title: 怎样向 AI 提出更容易得到高质量答案的问题？
entries.question: 我发现自己问 AI 的问题经常太宽泛，回答看起来很完整但用不上。有没有一种提问方式，能让 AI 给出更具体、可执行、能直接帮我推进工作的答案？
entries.answer: 可以把问题拆成四个部分：背景、目标、约束、输出格式。先告诉 AI 你正在做什么、为什么重要；再说明你希望它帮你完成哪一步；然后列出限制条件，比如时间、预算、技术栈、受众、不能做什么；最后指定你想要的交付物，比如清单、表格、代码、决策建议或下一步行动。一个更好的提问模板是：我正在做 X，目标是 Y，当前限制是 A/B/C。请帮我产出 Z，并解释你为什么这样排序。这样问的好处是，AI 不需要猜上下文，也更容易把答案压到你真正能用的形态。
entries.summary: 把好问题拆成背景、目标、约束和输出格式，让 AI 从泛泛回答转向可执行交付。
quality_signals: 问题来自真实使用痛点，不是抽象技巧讨论。
答案给出了可复用模板，能直接迁移到工作、学习和创作场景。
问题和回答都适合沉淀为公共知识卡片。

entries.title: What is the meaning of N in the description "The mean operation still operates over all the elements, and divides by N"?
entries.question: In torch.nn.MSELoss doc , it is mentioned that : where N is the batch size. Then : The mean operation still operates over all the elements, and divides by N . I am confused about the definition of N. According to my understanding, if the ground truth and predicted inputs are each of shape (B, C, H, W) (a batch of images, each of shape (C, H, W)), and MSE is used in this context as a reconstruction loss in an image reconstruction head with reduction = "mean", then N is defined as the total number of pixels = B × C × H × W. So here, N is the total number of pixels, not the batch size. So my question is: is my understanding of N in this use case correct?
entries.answer: Yes, reduction mean is equivalent of summing everything and dividing by the product of the resulting tensor

entries.title: Are there tail-aware strategies that keep tree-based boosting models from underpredicting extreme values at the tails of data?
entries.question: I’m facing a regression problem where rare extreme values dominate the real objective, and all tested models systematically underpredict them. Inputs are window statistical parameters of operational signals; the target is a pair of ordered global extremes per fixed window, later post‑processed into fatigue damage (highly nonlinear in amplitude). Histogram‑based gradient boosting, XGBoost/LightGBM, and linear AR models all fit the bulk distribution well (good RMSE/R²) but consistently shrink the upper tail, even after aggressive sample weighting (range‑based, power‑law, sequence‑aware), custom loss functions emphasizing tail errors (log‑space histogram loss, explicit underprediction penaltie...
entries.answer: Gradient boosting minimizes average loss across the distribution. Even with sample weights, the model's leaf values are means of samples in that leaf, so that means a leaf containing 95% normal values and 5% extremes will always predict something closer to the mean. So you may consider these Reframe as an Extreme Value Theory (EVT) problem Instead of regressing the raw target, fit the tail distribution using a Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) or Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD). Your model predicts the distribution parameters (location, scale, shape), and you sample or compute expected maxima from that. You can use the scipy.stats.genextreme and pyextremes libraries in python. Quantile regression targeting the upper tail Drop RMSE entirely. Train separate models for q=0.90, 0.95, 0.99 quantiles using pinball loss. Your fatigue damage estimate then uses the high quantile prediction rather than the mean. LightGBM has native quantile support (objective='quantile'). Two-stage model: bulk + extreme classifier Stage 1: binary classifier "is this window likely to contain an extreme?" Stage 2a: standard regressor for normal windows Stage 2b: separate regressor trained only on windows with confirmed extremes Are your input features themselves extreme during peak-stress windows, or are the extremes dynamically generated?
